job.title: Community Support Worker
job.description:
Pathway Talent is partnering with a respected community services organisation to recruit compassionate and reliable Community Support Workers in Dubbo.

This is a permanent part-time opportunity offering rostered shifts and meaningful work supporting people to live independently, participate in their community and achieve their individual goals.

About the Role As a Community Support Worker, you will provide person-centred support based on each customer’s individual needs, preferences and support plan.

Your responsibilities may include:
  • Supporting customers with daily living activities and personal care
  • Assisting with community access, appointments and social activities
  • Providing medication assistance in line with relevant procedures
  • Supporting customers to develop independence and practical life skills
  • Assisting with household tasks and meal preparation
  • Maintaining accurate case notes and documentation
  • Following individual support plans and positive behaviour support strategies
  • Promoting customer choice, dignity, safety and wellbeing
  • Working collaboratively with families, carers and other professionals
About You
You are compassionate, reliable and committed to supporting people to achieve meaningful outcomes. You understand the importance of professional boundaries and providing support that respects each person’s individual choices.

To be successful, you will have:
  • Previous experience in disability, mental health or community services
  • A person-centred and recovery-focused approach
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • The ability to work independently and respond calmly to changing situations
  • Good written communication and documentation skills
  • Flexibility to work rostered shifts, including mornings, afternoons, evenings, weekends and public holidays as required
Essential Requirements
  • Certificate III or IV in Individual Support, Disability, Mental Health or Community Services ( or willing to work towards)
  • Current NDIS Worker Screening Check
  • Working with Children Check, where required
  • Current First Aid and CPR certificates
  • Current Australian driver’s licence
  • Access to a reliable and insured vehicle
  • Australian working rights
  • Ability to meet the inherent requirements of the position
What’s on Offer
  • Permanent part-time employment
  • Guaranteed contracted hours
  • Rostered shifts across a seven-day service
  • SCHADS Award remuneration, plus applicable penalty rates and superannuation
  • Salary packaging benefits, where applicable
  • Ongoing training and professional development
  • A supportive and inclusive team environment
  • Meaningful work within the Dubbo community

Click Apply Now and submit your current resume. A member of the Pathway Talent team will contact shortlisted candidates to discuss the opportunity further.

job.title: Vocational Specialist
job.description:
Pathway Talent is partnering with a respected community-based mental health organisation to appoint a passionate and outcomes-focused Vocational Specialist within the Ashfield team.

This is a rewarding opportunity for an experienced employment services, vocational support or youth services professional seeking to help young people overcome barriers and achieve meaningful employment and education outcomes.

This is a full-time, max-term maternity leave contract ending June 2027, with the possibility of extension. The position is based in Ashfield area and works Monday to Friday.

About the Role

As the Vocational Specialist, you will support young people aged 12–25 who may be experiencing mental health challenges or other barriers to employment and education.

Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will deliver vocational support in line with the evidence-based model.

You will work closely with young people to understand their goals, identify suitable opportunities and connect them with employers, education providers and community services.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Supporting young people to identify and achieve their employment and education goals
  • Delivering individualised vocational assistance in line with the IPS model
  • Managing a caseload of young people and monitoring their progress
  • Building strong relationships with employers, employment services, education providers and community organisations
  • Proactively approaching employers to identify suitable employment opportunities
  • Promoting the IPS service to internal and external stakeholders
  • Establishing and maintaining effective referral pathways across the local community
  • Working collaboratively with clinical teams, families and other support networks
  • Maintaining accurate, timely and confidential case notes using the Best Practice electronic medical record system
  • Completing all required administration and documentation to a high standard
About You

You will be an empathetic, organised and proactive professional who is passionate about supporting young people to recognise their strengths and achieve their goals.

To be successful, you will bring:
  • Experience in employment services, job services, vocational support, career development, youth services, mental health or community services
  • Experience working with young people or other people experiencing vulnerability
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, partnership-building and negotiation skills
  • Confidence approaching and engaging employers to create employment opportunities
  • Strong administration, organisation and time-management skills
  • Excellent attention to detail when completing case notes and documentation
  • The ability to manage a caseload and balance competing priorities
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to contribute to a multidisciplinary team
  • Reliability, punctuality and a commitment to ethical, person-centred practice
  • Empathy, resilience and the ability to build trust with young people
A genuine passion for helping others and a willingness to learn are highly valued. ongoing training in the IPS model and relevant systems will be provided.

What’s on Offer
  • Full-time, max-term employment until June 2027 (possible extension)
  • Monday-to-Friday working hours
  • Salary packaging of up to $15,900 per FBT year
  • Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program
  • Internal and external learning, mentoring and training
  • Professional development 
  • Opportunities for continued career growth 
  • A supportive, collaborative and flexible working environment
  • Meaningful work supporting young people in the Ashfield community
Child Safety and Pre-Employment Screening Our client is committed to safeguarding children and young people and maintaining a child-safe environment.

This position involves child-related work. The successful candidate must hold a valid NSW Working with Children Check, which will be verified before commencement, and satisfactorily complete all other relevant pre-employment and probity checks.
  
Pathway Talent is committed to creating inclusive workplaces. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, culturally and linguistically diverse communities, LGBTQIA+ people and candidates of all ages.

How to Apply
 If you are passionate about helping young people overcome barriers and achieve meaningful employment or education outcomes, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Intake and Assessment Officer (SST)
job.description:

The SST program assists people experiencing mental health challenges and housing instability to maintain their tenancies, strengthen independence, and connect with the services and supports they need to thrive.

As an SST Intake & Assessment Officer, you will coordinate intake, assessment, referral, and service allocation processes to ensure participants receive the right support at the right time.

You will work closely with participants, community partners, support services, and internal teams to identify needs, assess risks, facilitate referrals, and create pathways to improved wellbeing and housing stability.

This role is ideal for someone who combines strong assessment and administrative capabilities with genuine compassion and a commitment to person-centred practice.

  • Coordinate participant onboarding and service allocation.
  • Facilitate referrals to appropriate internal and external supports.
  • Maintain accurate records, databases, case notes, and reporting requirements.
  • Build positive relationships with participants, community services, and key stakeholders.
  • Promote recovery-oriented and strengths-based approaches to service delivery.

  • Knowledge of recovery-oriented and person-centred practice.
  • Strong communication, engagement, and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent organisational, administrative, and time-management abilities.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining attention to detail.
  • A collaborative approach and commitment to achieving positive participant outcomes.
  • Qualifications in Community Services, Mental Health, Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

job.title: Aboriginal Caseworker (SST) | Coffs Harbour | Full-Time
job.description:

Finding and maintaining safe, secure housing is becoming increasingly difficult for many people in our communities. Whether someone is experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, or struggling to maintain an existing tenancy, having the right support can make a life-changing difference.

Pathway Talent is recruiting for an experienced and compassionate Aboriginal Caseworker to join a dedicated Supporting & Securing Tenancies (SST) program in Coffs Harbour.

You'll work alongside people facing complex challenges, providing practical support, advocacy and case management that creates meaningful and lasting outcomes.

Working collaboratively with clients, families, housing providers, community services and other stakeholders, you will assist people to navigate barriers, achieve their goals and maintain stable housing outcomes. You will develop support plans, coordinate services, advocate for clients, and empower individuals to build confidence, independence and a stronger future.

  • Develop, implement and review individual support plans
  • Advocate on behalf of clients and connect them to appropriate services

As an Inclusive Employment Support Worker / Process Worker, you will work alongside employees with disability within supported employment and production environments, providing coaching, guidance, and practical support to help them succeed at work.

job.title: Support Worker PPT Tweed Heads
job.description:
Make a meaningful difference

Pathway Talent is recruiting on behalf of a well-established for-purpose organisation with more than 55 years of experience supporting individuals, families and communities. 

About the role:
We are looking for an experienced Support Worker to provide services in our Tweed Heads region.
You will provide hands-on support to people living with disability in a home setting, assisting with personal care, meal preparation, medication, and daily living tasks while encouraging independence and choice.
This permanent part-time role offers 40 hours per fortnight across a 24/7 roster.
You'll build genuine relationships with customers and collaborate with their families and support team to ensure each person's individual goals and needs are met.
If you're caring, reliable, and want to make a real impact every day, we'd love to hear from you.

Your responsibilities:
  • Collaborate with customers to develop individualised person-centred support plans that incorporate their identified wellbeing needs, strengths and goals.
  • Provide support to customers to improve their independence by assisting with skill development, transport, social activities, supporting with finances, attending appointments, cooking, medication and personal care.
  • Support and encourage our customers to participate in activities of their choice, such as social, leisure, sporting, educational and employment activities
  • Keep customer records up to date on a daily basis using online systems and electronic databases.
  • Develop and maintain professional relationships and networks with customers, families, caregivers and key stakeholders.
  • Support customers to navigate the sector to access any additional service they may require.
  • Seek out innovative ways to enhance the recovery journey and overall customer experience.

  • Minimum Certificate III / Cert IV in Disability, Community or Mental Health and/or willingness to obtain.

job.description:
Disability Support Workers, Aged Care Workers & Mental Health Support Workers

Casual  and contract opportunities | From $45.28 per hour | Salary Packaging available

More than a job

At Pathway Talent, we’re redefining what it means to work in the disability and community support sector. As one of Australia’s not-for-profit staffing agencies specialising in Disability, Aged Care and Mental Health support, we connect compassionate people with meaningful work that helps others live independently, confidently, and with dignity.

About the Role

As a Support Worker, you will empower people from diverse backgrounds to achieve their goals, build independence, and stay connected with their communities.

We are looking for staff to provide NDIS, Icare and Aged Care support to individuals in their own home or in supported accomodation across multiple Regions of NSW. 

You will assist with a range of daily living activities, including (but not limited to) personal care, manual handling, meal preparation, medication administration, household tasks, community access, and transport. At all times, you will promote dignity, respect, and individual choice.


Why join Pathway Talent?
  • Great pay and benefits
    Earn from $45.28 per hour, and access to salary packaging to reduce your taxable income and increase your take home pay by up to $15,900, plus $2,650 for entertainment expenses. Enjoy novated leasing.
  • Flexible work on your terms
    Choose when, where, and how you work.
  • Ongoing training and professional development
    Grow through mentoring, skills training, and career development pathways.
  • Purpose above all else
    Be part of a community that values compassion, connection, and wellbeing.

  • Minimum Qualifications certificate III in Individual Support, Aged Care, Disability, Mental Health, AIN or equivalent;or 
  • University students welcome to apply (Allied Health, Nursing, OT, and related fields)
  • Experience in supporting clients with complex needs and behaviours (Desirable)
  • Current First Aid & CPR certification
  • Valid NSW Driver’s Licence
  • Working with Children Check
  • National Police Check (within 3 months)
  • NDIS Worker Screening Check and Orientation Module
  • Ability to lift up to 10kg unassisted
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • A heart full of empathy and a commitment to respect and dignity.
